title: Luyện Đọc VSTEP: Sleep and Human Health (VstepR3-Test 02)

tasks.instructions: Directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.

passage.title: Sleep and Human Health
passage.text:
Sleep is one of the most fundamental biological needs of the human body. During sleep, the brain consolidates memories, repairs neural connections, and processes the experiences of the day. The body also uses this time to repair tissues, produce hormones, and strengthen the immune system. Despite its critical importance, many people in modern society are chronically sleep-deprived, often sacrificing rest to meet the demands of work, school, or social activities.

Research has shown that insufficient sleep has serious consequences for both physical and mental health. People who regularly sleep fewer than seven hours per night are at higher risk for conditions including obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and depression. Cognitive functions such as attention, decision-making, and problem-solving are also impaired by sleep deprivation. Studies have found that sleep-deprived individuals perform as poorly as those who are legally intoxicated in tests of reaction time and judgment.

Given these findings, public health experts are increasingly calling for greater awareness of sleep hygiene — the set of practices that promote regular, high-quality sleep. These include maintaining a consistent sleep schedule, avoiding screens before bedtime, limiting caffeine consumption in the evening, and creating a dark, quiet sleeping environment. Schools and workplaces are also being encouraged to adjust their schedules to better align with natural sleep patterns, particularly for adolescents, who tend to have later natural sleep cycles than adults.
